items.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020
items.q: when we do Nancy Wilson, I just re-wrote her article that was maybe 350 or 400 words, now it’s probably a thousand, I didn’t count.

ctx.x: Yes. That’s a big factor. It takes off a lot of pressure because you don’t have to worry about publication cost. And you want to show some editorial sense as far as proportion and consistency and you don’t write 300 words about this person and 7000 about the next. You want to have a balance maintained, but you can add a lot of detail that I would have had to worry about twenty years ago and don’t have to worry about now. If it’s important I can put it in. I think the much bigger consideration now is it’s no…

Online, a component of Oxford Music Online. Which means when we do Nancy Wilson, I just re-wrote her article that was maybe 350 or 400 words, now it’s probably a thousand, I didn’t count. Because we’re no longer writing about Nancy Wilson as a jazz musician. We’re about writing about Nancy Wilson as a jazz musician, as a popular musician, as an actress, as an entertainer on TV, as a host of the “Jazz Profiles” show, as a civil rights activist, as a member of the Minority Council on AIDS. We’re writing about her…

Well Nancy would be happy, wherever she is, because as you heard her say in the session we did that she didn’t like to be called a jazz singer. She just felt she was a singer and let me choose what I want to do. I was so surprised when she said that the critics panned her record with Cannonball Adderley.
